title: Pairwise preferences: win rates, Elo and leaderboard
scenario: Raters compared model pairs across 12 collection rounds. Filter skipped, failed-rater and invalid comparisons, compute win rates with half-credit ties, run sequential Elo in numeric round order, and list models with at least 11 games.

verified.why_correct: `opponent - rating` in the exponent looks reversed, but it is the standard Elo formula from README rule 8: a stronger opponent makes the exponent positive and the expected score drop below 0.5.

bugs.title: Counter.update on a model name counts its letters
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_win_rates: every rate collapses to the tie credit only, e.g. m-alpha 0.042, m-beta 0.077, m-gamma 0.045 (should be 0.875 / 0.692 / 0.5). Games and exclusions are correct.
bugs.why: Counter.update iterates its argument, and iterating a string yields its characters, so the counts go to 'm', '-', 'a', … and no model ever has a win. Only the half-credit from ties is left.
hints: Every win rate equals half its tie share. Where did the wins go?
probes: Why does games.update(comp.models) work while wins.update(comp.winner) doesn't?
Why did Elo stay correct while this was present?

bugs.title: Round kept as text, so 10-12 sort before 2
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_elo_ratings: all ratings shift slightly, e.g. m-alpha 1107.4 vs 1118.7, m-beta 1075.9 vs 1062.0, m-gamma 994.9 vs 1000.4. The sum and the leaderboard order are unchanged.
bugs.why: elo_ratings sorts by `round`. As strings, '10', '11', '12' sort between '1' and '2', so rounds 10-12 are applied early. Elo is order-dependent, so every rating shifts slightly, though win rates and the leaderboard order don't change.
hints: Win rates are right but all Elo values are a little off. Elo depends on more than the counts. On what?
Check the type of Comparison.round when elo_ratings sorts by it.
Parse the round with int(...) in load_comparisons.
probes: Why didn't the sum of ratings change?
Would sorting by comparison_id have been safe instead? Why not?

bugs.title: Model with exactly the minimum games left off
bugs.old: eligible = [m for m in ratings if games[m] >= MIN_GAMES]
bugs.new: eligible = [m for m in ratings if games[m] > MIN_GAMES]
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_leaderboard: [m-alpha, m-beta, m-delta]; m-gamma (exactly 11 games) is missing.
bugs.why: The README says at least 11 games. m-gamma has exactly 11 and `>` drops it.
hints: Which model is missing from the leaderboard, and how many games did it play?
Compare the eligibility filter with README rule 10.
probes: m-eps is also missing in the expected output. Why is that correct?
What single data point would you add to a test to pin down this boundary?

context_qa.a: A list of valid `Comparison` objects in file order and a Counter of exclusion reasons (`skipped`, `rater`, `invalid`). For a tie, `winner` is None; otherwise it is the winning model's cleaned name.

context_qa.q: How are flags like skipped parsed?
context_qa.a: `flag()` returns JSON booleans as is; anything else is cleaned, lower-cased and checked against {true, yes, y, 1}.

It walks the comparisons and fills three Counters: `games` (both models), `ties` (both models on a tie) and `wins` (on a decisive result). The rate per model is (wins + 0.5 × ties) / games, rounded to 3 decimals. It returns (games, rates).

context_qa.q: In what order does elo_ratings apply comparisons?
context_qa.a: It sorts the valid comparisons with `key=lambda c: c.round`; sorting is stable, so within the same round value the file order is kept.

context_qa.q: Where is the minimum-games rule applied?
context_qa.a: In `reports.leaderboard`, which filters models by `games[m]` against `MIN_GAMES` (11) and sorts the rest by (-rating, name). Elo and win rates are still reported for every model.
Yes. Model a gains K × (Sa − Ea) and model b gains K × ((1 − Sa) − (1 − Ea)), which is the negative of a's change, so the ratings always add up to 1000 × the number of models.
